title: The Relayer role belongs to an off-chain ALM Planner system rather than a human trader
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.2 defines the role precisely: "The `RELAYER_ROLE` is the address for the Spark Liquidity Layer **ALM Planner off-chain system** that calls functions on `Controller` contracts to perform actions on behalf of the `ALMProxy` contract."

The privileged actor in day-to-day capital movement is therefore a program. Allocation decisions are computed off-chain by the Planner — which can read positions, rates and target balances across every chain — and executed on-chain within the ALM contracts' limits.

This explains several design choices elsewhere. Rate limits as replenishing buckets are the natural way to bound an automated agent that acts continuously. Minimum operation sizes make sense as a rule given to a planner that would otherwise optimize away small differences at uneconomic cost. And target balance bands are inputs to a planning algorithm, not instructions to a person.

It also relocates the trust question. The relevant risk is not primarily a rogue operator but a faulty or manipulated planner: bad input data, a mis-specified objective, or a compromised deployment producing well-formed but harmful transactions. The on-chain answer is that the Planner's authority is a bounded envelope, and the Freezer — which can revoke the Relayer role outright — is the kill switch when the automation misbehaves.
description: RELAYER_ROLE is defined as the address for the Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Planner, which calls Controller functions on behalf of the ALMProxy — automation acting inside on-chain limits.
